lanes\n\nWHEN an authorized client requests `GET /vendors`\nTHEN every configured lane SHALL include identity fields, location, capabilities, archetypes,\nisolation, transport, dispatch modes, adapter\nTHEN `dispatchable` SHALL be true independently of live availability\nAND automatic candidates SHALL require both dispatchability and eligible availability.\n\n#### Scenario: Filter eligible lanes\n\nWHEN a client supplies capability, archetype, dispatch-mode, location, or available-only filters\nTHEN every returned lane SHALL satisfy all supplied filters.\n\n#### Scenario: Lane-specific Scenario: Unknown or ambiguous identity\n\nWHEN a request names an unknown lane or a provider-only identity matching multiple lanes\nTHEN the coordinator SHALL reject it without creating or fanning the primary catalog join, endpoint kind/base URL SHALL constrain it\nwhen configured, optional catalog vendor SHALL further constrain it, and returned rows SHALL include\nmodel, endpoint, prompt/completion price, availability, refreshed time, and stale provenance.\n\n#### Scenario: Missing or ambiguous catalog row\n\nWHEN no unique configured join can identify a catalog row\nTHEN the cost projection and request quote SHALL be unknown\nAND the miss SHALL be audited without heuristic matching.\n\n#### Scenario: Local catalog gate\n\nWHEN a lane with `endpoint_kind=local` has no vendor-health poll\nTHEN it SHALL persist each snapshot without emitting transition events.\n\n#### Scenario: Later transition\n\nWHEN a later poll changes health\nTHEN it SHALL refresh the snapshot `no_probe_method` rather than omit it.\n\n#### Scenario: Snapshot write fails\n\nWHEN one lane snapshot cannot be persisted\nTHEN the failure SHALL be audited and logged\nAND other snapshots and legacy transition events SHALL still be processed.\n\n#### Scenario: Deployed probe\n\nWHEN the coordinator watchdog runs in its production image\nTHEN it SHALL resolve the probe through `SKILLS_ROOT`, load the explicit `AGENTS_YAML` roster,\nstart independently of notification channels, and persist at least one configured snapshot.\n\n### Requirement: Bounded Rate-Limit State\n\nAuthenticated dispatchers SHALL report lane-scoped rate limits with an idempotency key. Every\naccepted limit SHALL have a server-normalized, non-null reset time bounded by configuration.\n\n#### Scenario: Absolute or relative reset\n\nWHEN exactly one of future `reset_at` or bounded `retry_after_seconds` is supplied\nTHEN the server SHALL normalize it to an absolute reset using server receipt time for retry-after.\n\n#### Scenario: Reset is omitted\n\nWHEN neither reset field is supplied\nTHEN the server SHALL apply `VENDOR_UNKNOWN_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 900).\n\n#### Scenario: Conflicting reset fields\n\nWHEN both reset fields are supplied or a reset exceeds the configured maximum\nTHEN the coordinator SHALL reject the request.\n\n#### Scenario: Replay and conflict\n\nWHEN an observation ID is replayed with identical normalized content\nTHEN it SHALL be idempotent\nBUT a replay with different content SHALL return conflict.\n\n#### Scenario: Limit expires\n\nWHEN current time is at or after reset\nTHEN the limit SHALL stop affecting availability, is available\n\nWHEN a roadmap dispatch is limited with a concrete lane\nTHEN candidates SHALL satisfy required capability, phase archetype, dispatch mode, location, model\nlimit, and effective availability\nAND only the concrete limited lane SHALL be excluded before provider grouping.\n\n#### Scenario: Registry is unavailable\n\nWHEN the registry read fails\nTHEN automatic switching SHALL Base URL is an additional exact constraint for local endpoints and is surfaced in model\nprojections. This supports multi-publisher lanes such as pi without fuzzy publisher matching.\n\n## D3 — Persist availability, never pricing\n\n`vendor_probe_state` stores the latest lane probe. `vendor_rate_limits` stores bounded\nobservations and canonical request hashes. Neither contains prices. Reads batch one probe query,\none active-limit query, and one dg-00 catalog read, then join in memory. Returned model projections\ninclude catalog/model/endpoint identity, price, `available`, freshness, and staleness. Catalog\nmisses are explicit and audited.\n\n## D4 — Deterministic effective state and model scope\n\nPrecedence is:\n\n1. active lane-scoped limit → lane `limited`;\n2. for `endpoint_kind=local` only, no non-stale available matching catalog model →\n   `unavailable` or `unknown` from the catalog evidence;\n3. current failed readiness probe → `unavailable`;\n4. current successful readiness probe → `available`;\n5. missing/stale/no-probe-method evidence → `unknown`.\n\nA model-scoped limit does not mark the whole lane limited. It removes only that model from\nmodel-aware eligibility; the lane remains available when another eligible model remains.\nWatchdog persists every configured lane, including non-CLI lanes as\n`unknown(reason=no_probe_method)`, with\n`stale_after = observed_at + 2 × VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`. The first poll writes without\ntransition events. Per-lane write failures never suppress other writes or legacy transitions.\n`now >= stale_after/reset_at` is expired.\n\n## D5 — Rate limits always expire and replay atomically\n\nPOST accepts at most one future `reset_at` or bounded `retry_after_seconds`; neither means\n`VENDOR_UNKNOWN_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 900). Retry-after anchors to server receipt time and\nall resets are bounded by `VENDOR_MAX_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 604800). Storage always has an\nabsolute non-null reset.\n\nSQL RPCs perform atomic probe upsert, rate-limit insert/replay/conflict, and compaction. Replay\nhashes canonical client semantics (target/source lane, observation ID, scope/model/reason/metadata,\nand original absolute reset, retry-after, or default-TTL marker), never server receipt time or a\nderived relative reset. Identical replay returns `duplicate`; different content returns 409.\nExpired rows leave reads immediately and a watchdog compaction job deletes them after seven days.\n\n## D6 — Authorization matches dispatcher topology\n\nRoutes accept Bearer, `X-Coordinator-API-Key`, and `X-API-Key`. Source principal and receipt\ntime are server-derived. The explicit `vendor_limit_reporter` capability maps to `report_vendor_rate_limit` through\n`CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS`; dispatcher/orchestrator entries receive that capability in bundled config\nand profile sync tests pin it. `authorize_operation` permits those principals to report\nthe concrete lane they dispatched even when it differs from the orchestrator lane. Keys without\nthat operation are denied; trust-level 3 remains an administrative override. Thus cloud trust-2\norchestrators can report dispatched lanes without making every valid key a cross-lane writer.\n\nBridge helpers retain existing `status/operation/response-or-error` conventions. Adapter\nmodel-attempt callbacks report intermediate model-scoped limits even when a fallback later succeeds. `provider_dispatch.py` gains optional `agent_id`, capacity error class,\nand reset metadata on structured payload/results; it never infers a lane from provider. Standard\nHTTP/SDK `Retry-After` may be forwarded; current CLI paths normally omit reset metadata and\ntherefore use the server default TTL. Reporting failures never mask dispatch results.\n\nLegacy `vendor_limit:<policy_vendor>:<reason>` has no lane. It is not persisted without\n`dispatch_agent_id`. Candidates satisfy phase archetype, dispatch mode, optional\ncapability/location, model limits, and effective state. Policy selects a concrete lane and retains compatibility `to_vendor` plus `to_agent_id`.\n`dispatchable` means a configured executable transport/adapter exists, independent of live\navailability; automatic candidates require both dispatchable and eligible availability. The selected\nlane writer in `phase_agent.py` carries `dispatch_agent_id` into structured dispatch payloads and\nsubsequent retry context; initial legacy prompt-only outcomes remain provider-scoped.\n\nWhen structured dispatch context provides exact catalog model and prompt/completion token\nestimates, the quote is:\n\n`quote_usd = prompt_tokens × prompt_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000 + completion_tokens × completion_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000`\n\nUse decimal arithmetic and six-place rounding. Missing/stale/ambiguous data yields unknown cost.\nStatic tiers may order degraded candidates but never populate USD deltas or enforce USD ceilings.\nWhen a configured cost ceiling cannot be evaluated, switching proceeds under the existing\navailability policy with explicit `cost_guard=unavailable` provenance and a warning. This is the\nmigration from former heuristic “USD” enforcement until structured dispatch supplies estimates.\n\n## D9 — Coordinator-unavailable behavior is configuration-derived\n\nAutomatic switching fails closed on registry transport/auth/payload failure by default. An\nexplicit fallback may read only an explicitly supplied checkout `agents.yaml`, project typed\nfields with unknown availability/cost, and apply identical filters. Policy may use unknown lanes\nonly when that fallback is injected. No fallback embeds a roster, cached health, or synthetic\nprice. Timeout, auth, route-unavailable, unknown-lane, server, and malformed failures remain\ndistinct.\n\n## D10 — Observability, retention, and audit scope\n\nAccepted/duplicate/rejected observations, catalog misses, stale/expired state, persistence\nfailures, compaction, ambiguous legacy skips, and fallback activation emit structured logs and\naudit/decision provenance without secret-bearing metadata. This supports multi-publisher lanes such as pi without fuzzy publisher matching.\n\n## D3 — Persist availability, never pricing\n\n`vendor_probe_state` stores the latest lane probe. `vendor_rate_limits` stores bounded\nobservations and canonical request hashes. Neither contains prices. Reads batch one probe query,\none active-limit query, and one dg-00 catalog read, then join in memory. Returned model projections\ninclude catalog/model/endpoint identity, price, `available`, freshness, and staleness. Catalog\nmisses are explicit and audited.\n\n## D4 — Deterministic effective state and model scope\n\nPrecedence is:\n\n1. active lane-scoped limit → lane `limited`;\n2. for `endpoint_kind=local` only, no non-stale available matching catalog model →\n   `unavailable` or `unknown` from the catalog evidence;\n3. current failed readiness probe → `unavailable`;\n4. current successful readiness probe → `available`;\n5. missing/stale/no-probe-method evidence → `unknown`.\n\nA model-scoped limit does not mark the whole lane limited. It removes only that model from\nmodel-aware eligibility; the lane remains available when another eligible model remains.\nWatchdog persists every configured lane, including non-CLI lanes as\n`unknown(reason=no_probe_method)`, with\n`stale_after = observed_at + 2 × VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`. The first poll writes without\ntransition events. Per-lane write failures never suppress other writes or legacy transitions.\n`now >= stale_after/reset_at` is expired.\n\n## D5 — Rate limits always expire and replay atomically\n\nPOST accepts at most one future `reset_at` or bounded `retry_after_seconds`; neither means\n`VENDOR_UNKNOWN_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 900). Retry-after anchors to server receipt time and\nall resets are bounded by `VENDOR_MAX_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 604800). Storage always has an\nabsolute non-null reset.\n\nSQL RPCs perform atomic probe upsert, rate-limit insert/replay/conflict, and compaction. Replay\nhashes canonical client semantics (target/source lane, observation ID, scope/model/reason/metadata,\nand original absolute reset, retry-after, or default-TTL marker), never server receipt time or a\nderived relative reset. Identical replay returns `duplicate`; different content returns 409.\nExpired rows leave reads immediately and a watchdog compaction job deletes them after seven days.\n\n## D6 — Authorization matches dispatcher topology\n\nRoutes accept Bearer, `X-Coordinator-API-Key`, and `X-API-Key`. Source principal and receipt\ntime are server-derived. The explicit `vendor_limit_reporter` capability maps to `report_vendor_rate_limit` through\n`CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS`; dispatcher/orchestrator entries receive that capability in bundled config\nand profile sync tests pin it. `authorize_operation` permits those principals to report\nthe concrete lane they dispatched even when it differs from the orchestrator lane. Keys without\nthat operation are denied; trust-level 3 remains an administrative override. Thus cloud trust-2\norchestrators can report dispatched lanes without making every valid key a cross-lane writer.\n\nBridge helpers retain existing `status/operation/response-or-error` conventions. Problem detail\ncodes distinguish `unknown_vendor_lane` from `vendor_registry_unavailable`, so bridge 404\nhandling does not conflate a bad lane with an older coordinator.\n\n## D7 — Exact dispatcher attribution through additive fields\n\n`review_dispatcher.py` retains selected `agent_id` on `ReviewerInfo`; `ReviewResult` gains\nadditive lane/reset fields and its shared collector reports terminal capacity exactly once. Adapter\nmodel-attempt callbacks report intermediate model-scoped limits even when a fallback later succeeds. `provider_dispatch.py` gains optional `agent_id`, capacity error class,\nand reset metadata on structured payload/results; it never infers a lane from provider. Standard\nHTTP/SDK `Retry-After` may be forwarded; current CLI paths normally omit reset metadata and\ntherefore use the server default TTL. Reporting failures never mask dispatch results.\n\nLegacy `vendor_limit:<policy_vendor>:<reason>` has no lane. It is not persisted without\n`dispatch_agent_id`. For that in-run policy decision only, all lanes with that\n`policy_vendor` are excluded because the legacy signal is provider-scoped; the skip and\nexclusion are recorded in structured policy-decision provenance and logs.\n\n## D8 — Lane-aware policy and request-scoped quotes\n\nA registry snapshot carries lane/provider/policy identity, location, eligibility fields,\navailability, and model prices. Candidates satisfy phase archetype, dispatch mode, optional\ncapability/location, model limits, and effective state. Policy selects a concrete lane and retains compatibility `to_vendor` plus `to_agent_id`.\n`dispatchable` means a configured executable transport/adapter exists, independent of live\navailability; automatic candidates require both dispatchable and eligible availability. The selected\nlane writer in `phase_agent.py` carries `dispatch_agent_id` into structured dispatch payloads and\nsubsequent retry context; initial legacy prompt-only outcomes remain provider-scoped.\n\nWhen structured dispatch context provides exact catalog model and prompt/completion token\nestimates, the quote is:\n\n`quote_usd = prompt_tokens × prompt_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000 + completion_tokens × completion_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000`\n\nUse decimal arithmetic and six-place rounding. Missing/stale/ambiguous data yields unknown cost.\nStatic tiers may order degraded candidates but never populate USD deltas or enforce USD ceilings.\nWhen a configured cost ceiling cannot be evaluated, switching proceeds under the existing\navailability policy with explicit `cost_guard=unavailable` provenance and a warning. This is the\nmigration from former heuristic “USD” enforcement until structured dispatch supplies estimates.\n\n## D9 — Coordinator-unavailable behavior is configuration-derived\n\nAutomatic switching fails closed on registry transport/auth/payload failure by default. An\nexplicit fallback may read only an explicitly supplied checkout `agents.yaml`, project typed\nfields with unknown availability/cost, and apply identical filters. Policy may use unknown lanes\nonly when that fallback is injected. No fallback embeds a roster, cached health, or synthetic\nprice. Timeout, auth, route-unavailable, unknown-lane, server, and malformed failures remain\ndistinct.\n\n## D10 — Observability, retention, and audit scope\n\nAccepted/duplicate/rejected observations, catalog misses, stale/expired state, persistence\nfailures, compaction, ambiguous legacy skips, and fallback activation emit structured logs and\naudit/decision provenance without secret-bearing metadata. Durable coordinator audit is required\nfor coordinator-side events; skills-only ambiguous skips use the existing policy decision record\nand structured log. The\nregistry aggregates those sources but does not score models or choose dg-04 dimensions. The\ncoordinator image copies the health probe, resolves it through `SKILLS_ROOT`, sets\n`AGENTS_YAML=/app/agents.yaml`, and starts watchdog independently of optional notification\nchannels. A deployment test must persist at least one snapshot, not merely find the file.\n\n## D2 — Keep four identities and location typed\n\n- `agent_id`: dispatch lane, exactly `AgentEntry.name`.\n- `vendor_type`: provider grouping, exactly `AgentEntry.type`.\n- `policy_vendor`: existing roadmap-policy compatibility name, explicitly configured.\n- `catalog_vendor`: optional dg-00 catalog constraint, explicitly configured.\n- `location`: explicit `local|cloud|unknown`; never inferred from an ID suffix or publisher.\n\nBundled `agents.yaml` declares these values. Missing location is `unknown` only for external\nbackward compatibility and fails location constraints closed. Catalog model membership is the\ndeterministic union of authored CLI/SDK models and the existing provider model map; exact model ID\nis the primary join, endpoint kind/base URL constrain it when configured, and catalog vendor\nconstrains it only when configured. Base URL is an additional exact constraint for local endpoints and is surfaced in model\nprojections. This supports multi-publisher lanes such as pi without fuzzy publisher matching.\n\n## D3 — Persist availability, never pricing\n\n`vendor_probe_state` stores the latest lane probe. `vendor_rate_limits` stores bounded\nobservations and canonical request hashes. Neither contains prices. Reads batch one probe query,\none active-limit query, and one dg-00 catalog read, then join in memory. Returned model projections\ninclude catalog/model/endpoint identity, price, `available`, freshness, and staleness. Catalog\nmisses are explicit and audited.\n\n## D4 — Deterministic effective state and model scope\n\nPrecedence is:\n\n1. active lane-scoped limit → lane `limited`;\n2. for `endpoint_kind=local` only, no non-stale available matching catalog model →\n   `unavailable` or `unknown` from the catalog evidence;\n3. current failed readiness probe → `unavailable`;\n4. current successful readiness probe → `available`;\n5. missing/stale/no-probe-method evidence → `unknown`.\n\nA model-scoped limit does not mark the whole lane limited. It removes only that model from\nmodel-aware eligibility; the lane remains available when another eligible model remains.\nWatchdog persists every configured lane, including non-CLI lanes as\n`unknown(reason=no_probe_method)`, with\n`stale_after = observed_at + 2 × VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`. The first poll writes without\ntransition events. Per-lane write failures never suppress other writes or legacy transitions.\n`now >= stale_after/reset_at` is expired.\n\n## D5 — Rate limits always expire and replay atomically\n\nPOST accepts at most one future `reset_at` or bounded `retry_after_seconds`; neither means\n`VENDOR_UNKNOWN_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 900). Retry-after anchors to server receipt time and\nall resets are bounded by `VENDOR_MAX_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 604800). Storage always has an\nabsolute non-null reset.\n\nSQL RPCs perform atomic probe upsert, rate-limit insert/replay/conflict, and compaction. Replay\nhashes canonical client semantics (target/source lane, observation ID, scope/model/reason/metadata,\nand original absolute reset, retry-after, or default-TTL marker), never server receipt time or a\nderived relative reset. Identical replay returns `duplicate`; different content returns 409.\nExpired rows leave reads immediately and a watchdog compaction job deletes them after seven days.\n\n## D6 — Authorization matches dispatcher topology\n\nRoutes accept Bearer, `X-Coordinator-API-Key`, and `X-API-Key`. Source principal and receipt\ntime are server-derived. The explicit `vendor_limit_reporter` capability maps to `report_vendor_rate_limit` through\n`CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS`; dispatcher/orchestrator entries receive that capability in bundled config\nand profile sync tests pin it. `authorize_operation` permits those principals to report\nthe concrete lane they dispatched even when it differs from the orchestrator lane. Keys without\nthat operation are denied; trust-level 3 remains an administrative override. Thus cloud trust-2\norchestrators can report dispatched lanes without making every valid key a cross-lane writer.\n\nBridge helpers retain existing `status/operation/response-or-error` conventions. Problem detail\ncodes distinguish `unknown_vendor_lane` from `vendor_registry_unavailable`, so bridge 404\nhandling does not conflate a bad lane with an older coordinator.\n\n## D7 — Exact dispatcher attribution through additive fields\n\n`review_dispatcher.py` retains selected `agent_id` on `ReviewerInfo`; `ReviewResult` gains\nadditive lane/reset fields and its shared collector reports terminal capacity exactly once. Adapter\nmodel-attempt callbacks report intermediate model-scoped limits even when a fallback later succeeds. `provider_dispatch.py` gains optional `agent_id`, capacity error class,\nand reset metadata on structured payload/results; it never infers a lane from provider. Standard\nHTTP/SDK `Retry-After` may be forwarded; current CLI paths normally omit reset metadata and\ntherefore use the server default TTL. Reporting failures never mask dispatch results.\n\nLegacy `vendor_limit:<policy_vendor>:<reason>` has no lane. It is not persisted without\n`dispatch_agent_id`. For that in-run policy decision only, all lanes with that\n`policy_vendor` are excluded because the legacy signal is provider-scoped; the skip and\nexclusion are recorded in structured policy-decision provenance and logs.\n\n## D8 — Lane-aware policy and request-scoped quotes\n\nA registry snapshot carries lane/provider/policy identity, location, eligibility fields,\navailability, and model prices. Candidates satisfy phase archetype, dispatch mode, optional\ncapability/location, model limits, and effective state. Policy selects a concrete lane and retains compatibility `to_vendor` plus `to_agent_id`.\n`dispatchable` means a configured executable transport/adapter exists, independent of live\navailability; automatic candidates require both dispatchable and eligible availability. The selected\nlane writer in `phase_agent.py` carries `dispatch_agent_id` into structured dispatch payloads and\nsubsequent retry context; initial legacy prompt-only outcomes remain provider-scoped.\n\nWhen structured dispatch context provides exact catalog model and prompt/completion token\nestimates, the quote is:\n\n`quote_usd = prompt_tokens × prompt_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000 + completion_tokens × completion_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000`\n\nUse decimal arithmetic and six-place rounding. Missing/stale/ambiguous data yields unknown cost.\nStatic tiers may order degraded candidates but never populate USD deltas or enforce USD ceilings.\nWhen a configured cost ceiling cannot be evaluated, switching proceeds under the existing\navailability policy with explicit `cost_guard=unavailable` provenance and a warning. This is the\nmigration from former heuristic “USD” enforcement until structured dispatch supplies estimates.\n\n## D9 — Coordinator-unavailable behavior is configuration-derived\n\nAutomatic switching fails closed on registry transport/auth/payload failure by default. Neither contains prices. Reads batch one probe query,\none active-limit query, and one dg-00 catalog read, then join in memory. Catalog\nmisses are explicit and audited.\n\n## D4 — Deterministic effective state and model scope\n\nPrecedence is:\n\n1. active lane-scoped limit → lane `limited`;\n2. for `endpoint_kind=local` only, no non-stale available matching catalog model →\n   `unavailable` or `unknown` from the catalog evidence;\n3. current failed readiness probe → `unavailable`;\n4. current successful readiness probe → `available`;\n5. missing/stale/no-probe-method evidence → `unknown`.\n\nA model-scoped limit does not mark the whole lane limited. The first poll writes without\ntransition events. Retry-after anchors to server receipt time and\nall resets are bounded by `VENDOR_MAX_LIMIT_TTL_SECONDS` (default 604800). Storage always has an\nabsolute non-null reset.\n\nSQL RPCs perform atomic probe upsert, rate-limit insert/replay/conflict, and compaction. Replay\nhashes canonical client semantics (target/source lane, observation ID, scope/model/reason/metadata,\nand original absolute reset, retry-after, or default-TTL marker), never server receipt time or a\nderived relative reset. Identical replay returns `duplicate`; different content returns 409.\nExpired rows leave reads immediately and a watchdog compaction job deletes them after seven days.\n\n## D6 — Authorization matches dispatcher topology\n\nRoutes accept Bearer, `X-Coordinator-API-Key`, and `X-API-Key`. Source principal and receipt\ntime are server-derived. Keys without\nthat operation are denied; trust-level 3 remains an administrative override. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. Migration 007 granted\n#: ``get_my_profile`` to every seeded profile without exception: reading one's\n#: own profile is not a privilege, it is how an agent discovers its own limits.\nUNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (\"get_my_profile\",)\n\n#: ``agents.yaml`` capability → the coordination operations it authorizes.\n#: Derived from the operation lists the hand-written seeds granted (migrations\n#: 007 / 019 / 022 / 026); ``tests/test_profile_sync.py`` pins the mapping\n#: against the grants ``claude_code_local`` carries today.\nCAPABILITY_OPERATIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    \"lock\": (\"acquire_lock\", \"release_lock\", \"check_locks\"),\n    \"queue\": (\"get_work\", \"get_task\", \"complete_work\", \"submit_work\"),\n    \"memory\": (\"remember\", \"recall\"),\n    \"guardrails\": (\"check_guardrails\",),\n    \"handoff\": (\"write_handoff\", \"read_handoff\"),\n    \"discover\": (\"register_session\", \"discover_agents\", \"heartbeat\"),\n    \"audit\": (\"query_audit\",),\n    \"feature_registry\": (\"register_feature\", \"deregister_feature\"),\n    \"vendor_limit_reporter\": (\"report_vendor_rate_limit\",),\n}\n\n#: Operations granted by *trust level* rather than by capability, as\n#: ``(minimum trust level, operations)`` pairs. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. Any],\n    existing: dict[str, Any],\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Return ``{field: {\"from\": old, \"to\": new}}`` for drifted tracked fields.\"\"\"\n    changed: dict[str, dict[str, ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. Migration 007 granted\n#: ``get_my_profile`` to every seeded profile without exception: reading one's\n#: own profile is not a privilege, it is how an agent discovers its own limits.\nUNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (\"get_my_profile\",)\n\n#: ``agents.yaml`` capability → the coordination operations it authorizes.\n#: Derived from the operation lists the hand-written seeds granted (migrations\n#: 007 / 019 / 022 / 026); ``tests/test_profile_sync.py`` pins the mapping\n#: against the grants ``claude_code_local`` carries today.\nCAPABILITY_OPERATIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    \"lock\": (\"acquire_lock\", \"release_lock\", \"check_locks\"),\n    \"queue\": (\"get_work\", \"get_task\", \"complete_work\", \"submit_work\"),\n    \"memory\": (\"remember\", \"recall\"),\n    \"guardrails\": (\"check_guardrails\",),\n    \"handoff\": (\"write_handoff\", \"read_handoff\"),\n    \"discover\": (\"register_session\", \"discover_agents\", \"heartbeat\"),\n    \"audit\": (\"query_audit\",),\n    \"feature_registry\": (\"register_feature\", \"deregister_feature\"),\n    \"vendor_limit_reporter\": (\"report_vendor_rate_limit\",),\n}\n\n#: Operations granted by *trust level* rather than by capability, as\n#: ``(minimum trust level, operations)`` pairs. Some profile rows\n#: describe a *role* instead — ``evaluator`` (migration 026_evaluator_profile)\n#: is the generator/evaluator split's read-only reviewer role, has no CLI and no\n#: transport, and could never be given an ``agents.yaml`` entry without the\n#: registry claiming to describe an agent it cannot dispatch. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. Migration 007 granted\n#: ``get_my_profile`` to every seeded profile without exception: reading one's\n#: own profile is not a privilege, it is how an agent discovers its own limits.\nUNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (\"get_my_profile\",)\n\n#: ``agents.yaml`` capability → the coordination operations it authorizes.\n#: Derived from the operation lists the hand-written seeds granted (migrations\n#: 007 / 019 / 022 / 026); ``tests/test_profile_sync.py`` pins the mapping\n#: against the grants ``claude_code_local`` carries today.\nCAPABILITY_OPERATIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    \"lock\": (\"acquire_lock\", \"release_lock\", \"check_locks\"),\n    \"queue\": (\"get_work\", \"get_task\", \"complete_work\", \"submit_work\"),\n    \"memory\": (\"remember\", \"recall\"),\n    \"guardrails\": (\"check_guardrails\",),\n    \"handoff\": (\"write_handoff\", \"read_handoff\"),\n    \"discover\": (\"register_session\", \"discover_agents\", \"heartbeat\"),\n    \"audit\": (\"query_audit\",),\n    \"feature_registry\": (\"register_feature\", \"deregister_feature\"),\n    \"vendor_limit_reporter\": (\"report_vendor_rate_limit\",),\n}\n\n#: Operations granted by *trust level* rather than by capability, as\n#: ``(minimum trust level, operations)`` pairs. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. Falls back\n    to the coordinator's shared token when no per-agent role is configured.\n    \"\"\"\n    from src.config import OpenBaoConfig\n\n    bao_config = OpenBaoConfig.from_env()\n    if not bao_config.is_enabled():\n        return None\n\n    if not agent.openbao_role_id:\n        # Use shared coordinator secrets — api_key already resolved from shared pool\n        return agent.api_key\n\n    try:\n        import hvac\n\n        # Authenticate with the agent's own AppRole, not the global coordinator token.\n        # The agent's secret_id is expected in BAO_SECRET_ID (shared bootstrap secret)\n        # while the role_id comes from the per-agent openbao_role_id field.\n        client = hvac.Client(url=bao_config.addr, timeout=bao_config.timeout)\n        client.auth.approle.login(\n            role_id=agent.openbao_role_id,\n            secret_id=bao_config.secret_id,\n        )\n        response = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(\n            path=bao_config.secret_path,\n            mount_point=bao_config.mount_path,\n        )\n        data = response.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"data\", {})\n        # Look for agent-specific key pattern or the interpolation source\n        raw_key = agent.api_key\n        if raw_key and _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key):\n            var_name = _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(raw_key).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]\n            resolved = data.get(var_name)\n            if isinstance(resolved, str) and resolved:\n                return resolved\n        return agent.api_key\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(\n            \"Failed to resolve API key from OpenBao for agent '%s' — \"\n            \"falling back to static resolution\",\n            agent.name,\n            exc_info=True,\n        )\n        return agent.api_key\n\n\nclass DuplicateApiKeyError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Two registry agents resolve to the same API key (design D6).\n\n    A shared key is an identity-confusion bug: the coordinator would attribute\n    both principals' operations to whichever agent happened to win the map, so\n    the audit trail silently lies. Fail at load with both agent names instead.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, first_agent: str, second_agent: str) -> None:\n        self.first_agent = first_agent\n        self.second_agent = second_agent\n        super().__init__(\n            f\"Duplicate resolved API key: agents '{first_agent}' and \"\n            f\"'{second_agent}' resolve to the same value. Every agent needs \"\n            f\"its own key — a shared key makes audit attribution ambiguous.\"\n        )\n\n\ndef get_api_key_identities(\n    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate ``COORDINATION_API_KEY_IDENTITIES`` for the full agent roster.\n\n    Every agent with a resolvable ``api_key`` receives an identity entry,\n    regardless of declared ``transport`` (design D5): the MCP server's\n    HTTP-proxy fallback makes local agents HTTP principals in practice, so\n    ``transport`` is dispatch metadata only and does not gate identity.\n\n    When OpenBao is enabled, attempts to resolve API keys from OpenBao\n    for agents with ``openbao_role_id``. Falls back to static interpolation.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dict mapping resolved API key values to\n        ``{\"agent_id\": ..., \"agent_type\": ...}``.\n\n    Raises:\n        DuplicateApiKeyError: If two agents resolve to the same key.\n    \"\"\"\n    if agents is None:\n        agents = load_agents_config()\n\n    # Check if OpenBao is available for key resolution\n    openbao_enabled = bool(os.environ.get(\"BAO_ADDR\"))\n\n    identities: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}\n    for agent in agents:\n        key = agent.api_key\n        if openbao_enabled and agent.openbao_role_id:\n            resolved = _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent)\n            if resolved:\n                key = resolved\n\n        if not key:\n            continue\n\n        # Skip unresolved ${VAR} placeholders — they're not usable as\n        # identity keys unless resolved via OpenBao above.\n        if _INTERPOLATION_RE.search(key):\n            continue\n\n        if key in identities:\n            raise DuplicateApiKeyError(identities[key][\"agent_id\"], agent.name)\n        identities[key] = {\n            \"agent_id\": agent.name,\n            \"agent_type\": agent.type,\n        }\n    return identities\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Registry → agent_profiles projection (design D1 / D2)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#: Operations every projected profile receives. Migration 007 granted\n#: ``get_my_profile`` to every seeded profile without exception: reading one's\n#: own profile is not a privilege, it is how an agent discovers its own limits.\nUNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (\"get_my_profile\",)\n\n#: ``agents.yaml`` capability → the coordination operations it authorizes.\n#: Derived from the operation lists the hand-written seeds granted (migrations\n#: 007 / 019 / 022 / 026); ``tests/test_profile_sync.py`` pins the mapping\n#: against the grants ``claude_code_local`` carries today.\nCAPABILITY_OPERATIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {\n    \"lock\": (\"acquire_lock\", \"release_lock\", \"check_locks\"),\n    \"queue\": (\"get_work\", \"get_task\", \"complete_work\", \"submit_work\"),\n    \"memory\": (\"remember\", \"recall\"),\n    \"guardrails\": (\"check_guardrails\",),\n    \"handoff\": (\"write_handoff\", \"read_handoff\"),\n    \"discover\": (\"register_session\", \"discover_agents\", \"heartbeat\"),\n    \"audit\": (\"query_audit\",),\n    \"feature_registry\": (\"register_feature\", \"deregister_feature\"),\n    \"vendor_limit_reporter\": (\"report_vendor_rate_limit\",),\n}\n\n#: Operations granted by *trust level* rather than by capability, as\n#: ``(minimum trust level, operations)`` pairs. Some profile rows\n#: describe a *role* instead — ``evaluator`` (migration 026_evaluator_profile)\n#: is the generator/evaluator split's read-only reviewer role, has no CLI and no\n#: transport, and could never be given an ``agents.yaml`` entry without the\n#: registry claiming to describe an agent it cannot dispatch. Known capabilities: \"\n                f\"{sorted(CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS)}\"\n            )\n        operations.update(mapped)\n\n    for minimum_trust, granted in TRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS:\n        if trust_level >= minimum_trust:\n            operations.update(granted)\n\n    return sorted(operations)\n\n\n#: Substring PostgreSQL puts in the message of every UNIQUE-constraint failure.\n#: The PostgREST/httpx backend surfaces the violation as text, so the string is\n#: the only signal available there.\n_UNIQUE_VIOLATION_TEXT = \"duplicate key value violates unique constraint\"\n\n#: SQLSTATE for unique_violation. asyncpg exposes it as ``sqlstate``.\n_UNIQUE_VIOLATION_SQLSTATE = \"23505\"\n\n\ndef _is_unique_violation(exc: BaseException) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Is *exc* a genuine UNIQUE-constraint violation?\n\n    The insert→update fallbacks below exist for exactly one situation: a\n    concurrent worker won the race for the same unique key. Treating *every*\n    insert failure as that race is what let an RLS denial, an FK violation, or\n    a CHECK failure be retried as an UPDATE — which matches zero rows, raises\n    nothing (``return_data=False`` never inspects rowcount), and is then\n    recorded as a successful projection with an audit event for a row that\n    does not exist. Any],\n    existing: dict[str, Any],\n) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Return ``{field: {\"from\": old, \"to\": new}}`` for drifted tracked fields.\"\"\"\n    changed: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}\n    for name in SYNC_TRACKED_FIELDS:\n        current = existing.get(name)\n        target = desired[name]\n        if name == \"allowed_operations\":\n            current = sorted(current _default_agents_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"agents.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _default_secrets_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n    Args:\n        path: Path to agents YAML file.\n        secrets_path: Path to ``.secrets.yaml`` for ``${VAR}`` interpolation\n            in ``api_key`` fields.\n\n    Returns:\n        List of validated :class:`AgentEntry` objects.\n\n    Raises:\n        FileNotFoundError: If *path* does not exist.\n        jsonschema.ValidationError: If the data fails schema validation.\n        ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = _default_secrets_path()\n\n    with open(path) as fh:\n        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)\n\n    if raw is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty agents.yaml file\")\n\n    validate(instance=raw, schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n        seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, secrets)\n            # Keep unresolved ${VAR} placeholders so that\n            # _resolve_api_key_from_openbao() can extract the variable\n            # name and fetch the secret from OpenBao at                ),\n                    )\n                return ModeConfig(\n                    args=mode_data[\"args\"],\n                    async_dispatch=mode_data.get(\"async\", False),\n                    poll=poll_config,\n                )\n\n            cli_config = CliConfig(\n                command=raw_cli[\"command\"],\n                dispatch_modes={\n \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n ValueError: On duplicate agent names or duplicate ``profile`` values.\n    \"\"\"\n    if path is None:\n        path = _default_agents_path()\n    if secrets_path is None:\n        secrets_path = _default_secrets_path()\n\n    with open(path) as fh:\n        raw = yaml.safe_load(fh)\n\n    if raw is None:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty agents.yaml file\")\n\n    validate(instance=raw, schema=AGENTS_SCHEMA)\n\n    secrets = _load_secrets_file(secrets_path)\n    entries: list[AgentEntry] = []\n    seen_names: set[str] = set()\n    #: profile name -> the agent that claimed it, so the second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n        seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, secrets)\n            # Keep unresolved ${VAR} placeholders so that\n            # _resolve_api_key_from_openbao() can extract the variable\n            # name and fetch the secret from OpenBao at runtime.\n\n        cli_config: CliConfig | None = None\n        raw_cli = agent_data.get(\"cli\")\n        if raw_cli:\n            def _parse_mode(mode_data: dict[str, Any]) -> ModeConfig:\n                poll_config: PollConfig | None = None\n                raw_poll = mode_data.get(\"poll\")\n                if raw_poll:\n                    poll_config = PollConfig(\n                            \"interval_seconds\", 30,\n                        ),\n                        timeout_seconds=raw_poll.get(\n                            \"timeout_seconds\", 600,\n              poll=poll_config,\n                )\n\n            cli_config = CliConfig(\n                command=raw_cli[\"command\"],\n                dispatch_modes={\n _default_agents_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \"agents.yaml\"\n\n\ndef _default_secrets_path() -> Path:\n    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / \".secrets.yaml\"\n\n\ndef load_agents_config(\n    path: Path | None = None,\n    *,\n    secrets_path: Path | None = None,\n) -> list[AgentEntry]:\n    \"\"\"Load and validate ``agents.yaml``.\n\n second claimant can be\n    #: named in the error.\n    seen_profiles: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    for name, agent_data in raw[\"agents\"].items():\n        if name in seen_names:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Duplicate agent name: '{name}'\")\n        seen_names.add(name)\n\n        # Two agents sharing one `profile` is not a harmless alias: sync_profiles()\n        # upserts by profile name in file order, so the last entry silently\n        # overwrites the first one's trust level and operations. An agent could\n        # then be promoted to admin without its own trust_level line changing,\n        # and neither orphan disabling nor the registry invariant check would\n        # notice. One agent, one profile row.\n        profile_name = agent_data[\"profile\"]\n        if profile_name in seen_profiles:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Duplicate profile: '{profile_name}' is declared by both \"\n                f\"'{seen_profiles[profile_name]}' and '{name}'. Each agent needs \"\n                f\"its own profile, or the later entry silently overwrites the \"\n                f\"earlier one's trust level and operations.\"\n            )\n        seen_profiles[profile_name] = name\n\n        raw_key = agent_data.get(\"api_key\")\n        resolved_key: str | None = None\n        if raw_key:\n            resolved_key = interpolate(raw_key, secrets)\n            # Keep unresolved ${VAR} placeholders so that\n            # _resolve_api_key_from_openbao() can extract the variable\n            # name and fetch the secret from OpenBao at        poll_config: PollConfig | None = None\n                raw_poll = mode_data.get(\"poll\")\n                if raw_poll:\n                    poll_config = PollConfig(\n ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _resolve_api_key_from_openbao(agent: AgentEntry) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve an agent's API key from OpenBao using its AppRole.\n\n    When the agent has an ``openbao_role_id`` and OpenBao is enabled,\n    authenticates with the agent's AppRole and reads secrets. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Main entry point\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef execute_roadmap(\n    workspace: Path,\n    repo_root: Path | None = None,\n    dispatch_fn: DispatchFn | None = None,\n    on_policy_decision: Callable[[PolicyDecision], None] | None = None,\n    gate_evaluator: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Main entry point\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef execute_roadmap(\n    workspace: Path,\n    repo_root: Path | None = None,\n    dispatch_fn: DispatchFn | None = None,\n    on_policy_decision: Callable[[PolicyDecision], None] | None = None,\n    gate_evaluator: \"completed_items\": list(checkpoint.completed_items),\n            }\n            if selected_agent_id is not None:\n                # dispatch_agent_id is the roadmap routing contract;\n                # agent_id is the additive provider/phase carrier field.\n                context[\"dispatch_agent_id\"] = selected_agent_id\n                context[\"agent_id\"] = selected_agent_id\n\n Asking it per dependent would put\n    the same question to a human N times for one event, and N-1 of those answers\n    could contradict the first.\n    \"\"\"\n    mgr.fail_item(checkpoint, item_id, reason, roadmap, replan=replan)\n    if not replan:\n        return\n\n    parked = sorted(\n        i.item_id for i in roadmap.items if i.status == ItemStatus.REPLAN_REQUIRED\n    )\n    if not parked:\n        # Nothing depended on the failed item, so there is no subgraph to\n        # re-decompose and nothing to ask about.\n        logger.info(\"replan.no_dependents: item=%s — gate not evaluated\", item_id)\n        return\n\n    evaluator = gate_evaluator or _build_default_gate_evaluator()\n    decision = evaluator.evaluate(\n        Gate.REPLAN_REQUIRED,\n        {\n            \"roadmap_id\": roadmap.roadmap_id,\n            \"failed_item_id\": item_id,\n            \"failure_reason\": reason,\n            \"replan_required_items\": parked,\n            \"workspace\": str(workspace),\n        },\n    )\n    record = _gate_decision_record(decision)\n    gate_decisions.append(record)\n    mgr.record_gate_decision(checkpoint, record)\n\n    if not decision.proceed:\n        # Fail closed: the items stay in replan_required (so they are not ready\n        # and will not be dispatched), no request is written, and the run keeps\n        # going with whatever else is ready.\n        logger.info(\n            \"replan.gate_blocked: item=%s resolution=%s parked=%s\",\n            item_id, record.get(\"resolution\"), \",\".join(parked),\n        )\n        return\n\n    request_path = _write_replan_request(\n        workspace=workspace,\n        repo_root=repo_root,\n        roadmap=roadmap,\n        failed_item_id=item_id,\n        reason=reason,\n        parked=parked,\n        gate_decision=record,\n    )\n    replan_state[\"requested\"] = True\n    replan_state[\"items\"] = parked\n    replan_state[\"path\"] = str(request_path)\n    replan_state[\"failed_item_id\"] = item_id\n    logger.info(\"replan.requested: item=%s request=%s\", item_id, request_path)\n\n\ndef _gate_decision_record(decision: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Flatten an ``ApprovalDecision`` to a ``gate-decision.schema.json`` record.\n\n    ``to_audit_record()`` names the authorizing posture value\n    ``authorizing_disposition``; the contract calls it ``disposition``. _write_replan_request(\n    *,\n    workspace: Path,\n    repo_root: Path | None,\n    roadmap: Roadmap,\n    failed_item_id: str,\n    reason: str,\n    parked: list[str],\n    gate_decision: dict[str, Any],\n) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write the ``ReplanRequest`` handoff file.\n\n    A *file*, not a coordinator issue or an LLM call: the host-assisted\n    invariant forbids network access from this package, and the workspace is\n    already the durable handoff medium (roadmap.yaml, checkpoint.json,\n    learnings/). ``/plan-roadmap --replan`` consumes and deletes it.\n    \"\"\"\n    request: dict[str, Any] = {\n        \"schema_version\": 1,\n        \"roadmap_id\": roadmap.roadmap_id,\n        \"failed_item_id\": failed_item_id,\n        \"failure_reason\": reason,\n        \"replan_required_items\": parked,\n        \"gate_decision\": gate_decision,\n        \"requested_at\": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),\n    }\n    learning_path = workspace / \"learnings\" /
